note: Layout inputs the Rosebud export does not carry, in plate px. A re-laid plate (any size) ships its own copy of this file; nothing in build_city.py assumes 5120x2880.
source: docs/pc-map-handoff 98d2cc5c crosshaven/build.py WALL (ref x5), plot table from the look-target README
plate_scale_note: World px per plate px: the whole plate (ground, layers, walkmask, heightmap, cell grid) is drawn this much bigger; characters keep their size. Least-squares over Mauro's item 8 ratios against Ironjaw (62.7 px tall, about 38 px wide): house 3x (median house 168 px), gate tower 4.5x (308 px), stall 1.75x (131 px), street 3.5 hero widths (68 px across). See CROSSHAVEN_CITY_BUILD.md.

ground_textures.scale_note: Coordinator review 1: cobble tile at 0.35x (a stone is a hero foot to shin across), grass at 0.7x; a second grass layer (rotated 90 deg, offset, 1.13x) blended by low-frequency noise breaks the clover repeat.
ground_textures.review3_note: Coordinator round 3: second grass layer at 0.6 contrast and 0.8 weight; very-low-frequency value/hue patches (+-6%); outside the walls 10% less saturation and 5% darker.

map_base_only.note: Mauro item 17: the map base first. These layers stay in layers.json with hidden=true and keep their walk footprints reserved; set map_base_only to {} to show them again.

thatch_swap.note: Mauro item 15: no thatched roofs in the city until Scenario Art repaints them.

plot_exclude.note: cathedral park inside the ring road (not residential)

ring_kit.note: Coordinator 17 Oct: wall kit v2 (docs/pc-map-handoff docs/pc/look_target/crosshaven_city/work/walls/kit2 + kit/tower). Ring on the 3 plate directions: N and S horizontal, four iso diagonals (slope +-0.5); E and W are corners. Modules are painted at hero = 156 px; all anchors in native module px. Pass --kit <dir with the module files>.

exit.note: the south road and the existing city_to_crossroads stub

tower.note: Round 15: Grok's tower v6 (docs/pc-map-handoff d761b9c9, 607x990): iso angle like Mauro's reference, v5 details, flared plinth. For every ring, corner and water-gate tower. base = the plinth ellipse centre (on the wall line or corner point); plinth_front = the ellipse front below it (the tower sorts there, so both run ends hide behind its body); body_radius = shaft half width (428/2), base_radius = plinth half width (605/2). scale_mul 1.179 = the gatehouses' scale (their towers are pixel copies), so every tower is the same size.

segment_neg.note: Round 15: Grok's colour-regraded v7 segment (same coursing and alpha), foot AO.

segment_pos.note: Round 15: Grok's colour-regraded v7 segment (same coursing and alpha), foot AO.

segment_flat.note: Round 15: Grok's colour-regraded v7 segment (same coursing and alpha), foot AO.

watergate_neg.note: Round 15: Grok's water gate v6 (1355x917), iso, a curtain over the river in the gatehouse style. scale_mul 1.0417 (550/528) puts its merlons on the diagonal runs' line. arch = the opening's centre on the foot line; the gate is placed so the arch sits on the channel. Its painted water is trimmed to the river channel (no pool).

gatehouse_neg.note: Round 15: Grok's diagonal gatehouse v7 (1632x1420), iso, towers are tower_v6 copies (far one 0.9 for depth). Anchored on the two plinth centres (art_slope = their line, -0.399; the curtain itself -0.3615). curtain_level puts the curtain foot on the line through the plinth bottoms.

gatehouse_flat.note: Round 15: Grok's horizontal gatehouse v7 (2448x1050), iso, towers are tower_v6 copies (990 px, same scale as the ring towers). The wall line runs through the plinth centres (y 852; both plinth bottoms at 987, so the towers already stand level). curtain_level lifts the curtain columns (between the plinths) so its foot (13 px low at the left, 46 px at the right) sits on the plinth-bottom line: the towers no longer float above the curtain and road. Round 16: erase_boxes trims a stepped base block that stuck out below the right plinth.

ring_kit.face_note: face_px (segments): front merlon top to foot, native px. Gatehouses with face_px and curtain_foot are fitted to the run's face; the kit3 gatehouses instead carry a parapet-matched art_slope and drop_px from the coordinator's metrics (gatehouse_v3_metrics.json).
ring_kit.exits_note: Coordinator review 7: every gate road runs on to the plate edge and ends in a gate stub to a region road (data). The city is outside the plane, so these are stubs, not seams; 'proposed' links follow the Crossroads road directions, 'placeholder' means undecided.

gate_road.note: Rounds 6-7: every gate road opens into a funnel on both sides of the arch: 0.65 x the tower-centre span at the gate (to the towers' inner faces), easing (smoothstep) to the road width over 0.5 gatehouse width; uneven, feathered edge; where it meets the streets already there, a 40 px fillet blends the join into one curve.

ring_kit.corner_note: Round 5: every ring corner keeps its tower so the two runs never meet in a bare cut, unless a gatehouse span covers the corner itself (the W gate). The near-gate rule applies to mid-edge towers.
ring_kit.taper_note: Round 8: measured on the kit PNGs (merlon-tip and foot envelopes, fitted lines). The diagonal segments' merlon line is not parallel to their foot (face 653 -> 601 px across the tile), so each column is scaled about the foot to a constant face (627 on both diagonals, 545 flat): the merlon and foot lines then run on through any cut. art_slope is the fitted foot slope.

tower_tuck.note: Round 15: the tower sorts at its plinth front, so both runs tuck half a body radius under it and their ends hide behind the tower body.

ring_kit.snap_note: Round 8: a gatehouse whose outer flanking tower stands within 1.5 tower widths of a ring corner slides along its edge so that tower stands on the corner (no doubled tower, no gap); the neighbour run ends under it.
ring_kit.foot_calibration_note: Rounds 8 and 15: base_left set so each module's drawn foot (fitted over the last 320 px of each run, the tile phase continuous along the edge) lies on the wall line; re-measured for the v7 segments.
ring_kit.flat_scale_note: Round 9: the flat N/S segment and the horizontal gatehouse are scaled uniformly by 1.179 (blocks keep their proportions) so the flat merlon line meets the diagonals' at the NE/SE corner towers. Measured in game: flat merlon tips 190.0 plate px above the foot, diagonals 222.9 (NE) and 225.2 (SE); 224/190 = 1.179 puts both corners within 2 px (627/545 = 1.15 from the art faces left 4-6 px).
ring_kit.gates_note: Round 10 (Mauro): the SE gate is removed; the SE wall runs closed. Land gates N, S, W, E plus the 2 water gates.

tower_place.note: Round 10 (Mauro): the tower straddles the wall: its axis on the wall centreline (or on the corner point), its base as in the v5 gatehouse (13 px under the foot line); the near run ends at the tower body's silhouette, drawn in front; the far run tucks behind the tower.

water_gate_towers.note: Rounds 10, 13, 14: every water gate is flanked by two towers placed from the block centre outward at the first spot where the whole tower base outline is on dry ground (sliding further out only to keep the rhythm even, the block end staying inside the footprint). The block is trimmed to between the tower axes and otherwise keeps its piers down to the ground and water; the tower draws in front of it.

stone_recolor.note: LAB colour transfer of the wall segments and water gates to the tower v6 stone (its shaft): lightness mean and spread (clamped 0.85-1.15), a*/b* mean, chroma clamped to the reference's (hue kept), statistics from stone pixels only, warm pixels only. Recolour only. Round 15: off; Grok's v7 segments and v6 water gates are regraded at source.

ring_kit.spacing_note: Round 10 (GOAL): an even rhythm per side; one spacing per side, the most even split of every stretch between fixed towers (corners, gatehouse towers, water-gate towers), between 1.8 and 3 wall heights (preferring 2.5). A water-gate tower that lands on a gatehouse tower or corner is that tower.

contact_shadows.note: Round 15: grounding. Wall feet: a feathered shadow on both sides, 45% at the foot, 40 px on the shadow side (away from the upper-left light of the painted art) and 15 px on the lit side. Towers and gatehouse towers: a tight shadow centred on the plinth (0.97 x the plinth radius), shifted only 6% toward the shadow side. Not across passages or the river.

ring_kit.tower_kinds_note: Round 14 (ready for tower v6): ring towers take modules.tower; a kind can name its own sprite with modules.tower_wall, modules.tower_corner or modules.tower_water_gate (file, base anchor, scale_mul), falling back to modules.tower. Gatehouses are modules.gatehouse_flat / gatehouse_neg / gatehouse_pos (file, anchors: wall_left, wall_right, arch, split, arch_open_x, drop_px, art_slope, scale_mul). Swapping in v6 is a data change plus re-measured anchors.

tower_rule.note: Rounds 15-16: fixed towers are the gatehouse towers, the water-gate flanks and the corners no gatehouse or water-gate tower closes; a mid-wall tower only on a stretch longer than 9.5 wall heights, at its midpoint: 12 towers.

foot_decals.note: Round 15: grass tufts, pebbles and dirt patches (existing world ground art) scattered over the visible foot line of every wall run and round the front of every plinth, drawn over the wall bottom so grass grows over the base; dirt patches lie on the ground. Not on passages, roads or the river.

ring_kit.polygon_note: Round 16: the flat N and S edges are exactly one v7 horizontal gatehouse long (758.6 plate px between its tower plinth centres), so both gatehouse towers are the corners there: no doubled corner tower. To keep the room inside (10 plots), the ring is 150 px taller (N 470, S 2450) and so a little wider on the diagonals; same iso slopes.
ring_kit.kit5_note: Round 16: ready for kit5 curtain-only pieces. A module may set anchors_json (JSON beside the PNG; foot_left/foot_right/arch/split/arch_open_x/...; layout keys override) and flank_towers: true (the gatehouse or water gate gets a tower module placed at each foot anchor, like ring towers).

greenery.note: Approved map-base greenery (docs/pc-map-handoff 5edc29a3 docs/pc/look_target/crosshaven_city/work/green; pass --green <dir>). Painted at hero = 156 px, bottom-centre anchored.

outer_forest.note: Coordinator rounds 2-3: dense clumps of 5-15 trees with overlapping crowns outside the walls (about 140), hugging the wall foot and thickening into woods toward the plate edges; a soft dark multiply blob under the clumps; approved oak and cypress only; roads/river/gate approaches/bridges clear.

lights.note: Coordinator review 5: warm lamp light at dusk and night. Head points are fractions of the lamp art (x from the left, y from the top). Halo and ground pool reuse the world lamp glow art, additive. Performance mode keeps them still (no flicker). Outside Performance mode each lamp also carries a 2D point light that lifts the night tint around it.

gate_clear.note: Round 5: no tree or cypress in a clear plaza at every gate and water gate, inside or out: an iso ellipse 1.8 gatehouse widths across (rx = 0.9 x width, ry = rx/2); flowers and low bushes stay; benches, lamps and planters stay out too. The outer woods are placed around these plazas.

wall_ring.note: kit modules at hero 156. Round 15: every tower is tower v6 at 1.179 (990 x 1.179 = 1167), the gatehouses' towers are pixel copies at the same scale.

remove_bridges_note: Round 10 (Mauro): the bridge just outside the NE water gate is removed (sprite, deck cells and the road stubs that only led to it). Its ends stay in the lattice fit so the grid does not move.

drop_streets.note: Round 10 (Mauro): the spur from the S plaza toward the removed SE gate dead-ended at the wall; it goes back to grass.
Round 15: the S plaza's tongue ran to the old bridge landing at the river; it goes back to grass (the plaza now leads to the moved bridge).
Round 16: the outer SW road ran along the foot of the S gate's left tower and crossed the wall line; it now joins the gate funnel lower down.
Round 16: a street stub inside, against the S gate's left tower.

move_bridges_note: Round 15 (Mauro): the inner bridge behind the S gate landed on the gatehouse's right tower; both inner bridges slide 8 cells upstream (whole cells keep the decks on the lattice), so the S gate opens onto a small plaza and a short street to the bridge.

bridge_links.note: Round 15: the S gate opens onto a small plaza (its road mouth) and a short street to the moved bridge's south stair.

extra_roads.note: Round 16: the outer SW road joins the S gate funnel with a smooth curve, clear of the wall.
